framework.name: Illinois Learning Standards for Mathematics (Common Core State Standards for Mathematics)
framework.note: Codes are Common Core State Standards for Mathematics identifiers (e.g. 2.NBT.B.5, HSA-REI.B.4) as adopted by Illinois; the alignment is the course author's judgment and is not a certification.

standards.text: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Pair each object with one number name and understand the last number said tells how many.
Decide whether one group has more, fewer or the same number of objects as another.
See a two-digit number as some tens and some ones, with ten as a bundle of ten ones.
Compare two two-digit numbers by their tens and ones using >, = and <.
Mentally find ten more or ten less than a two-digit number and explain why.
Show addition as putting together or adding to and subtraction as taking apart or taking from, with objects and drawings.
Solve add-and-subtract word problems within 20 with the unknown in any position.
Add and subtract within 20 using strategies such as counting on, making ten and doubles.
Understand that the equal sign means both sides are the same amount.
Solve one- and two-step word problems within 100 involving addition and subtraction.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently, knowing sums of two one-digit numbers from memory.
Understand a three-digit number as amounts of hundreds, tens and ones.
Read and write numbers to 1,000 in numerals, words and expanded form.
Compare two three-digit numbers by place value using >, = and <.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently using place value and properties of operations.
Add and subtract within 1,000 with models and drawings, regrouping when needed.
Decide whether a group of objects is even or odd.
Measure a length by laying same-size units end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
Measure lengths choosing suitable tools such as rulers, yardsticks and meter sticks.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes on analog and digital clocks, using a.m. and p.m.
Solve word problems with dollars, quarters, dimes, nickels and pennies.
Measure lengths and show the data on a line plot.
Make picture graphs and bar graphs and answer questions from them.
Name shapes correctly no matter their size or how they are turned.
Tell defining attributes such as sides and corners from non-defining ones like color or size.
Put together two- and three-dimensional shapes to make new shapes.
Recognize and draw shapes with a given number of sides, angles or faces.
Divide a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count them.
Partition circles and rectangles into halves, thirds and fourths and describe the equal shares.
Interpret a product of whole numbers as a number of equal groups.
Interpret a quotient as sharing into equal groups or finding how many groups.
Use the commutative, associative and distributive properties to multiply and divide.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently, knowing single-digit products from memory.
Solve two-step word problems with the four operations and check answers by estimating.
Solve multi-step word problems with whole numbers, interpreting any remainder.
Recognize that each place is ten times the value of the place to its right.
Read, write and compare multi-digit numbers in numerals, words and expanded form.
Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently with the standard algorithm.
Multiply multi-digit numbers using place value, area models and partial products.
Divide whole numbers with up to four-digit dividends and two-digit divisors, explaining the method.
Represent fractions as points on a number line built from unit fractions.
Explain fraction equivalence and compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, including in word problems.
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators by finding equivalent fractions.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number or a fraction, using area models.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions with models and stories.
Write fractions with denominators 10 and 100 as decimals.
Compare two decimals to hundredths and record with >, = or <.
Explain patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of ten, including decimal-point shifts.
Read, write and compare decimals to thousandths using place value.
Round decimals to any place.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths with models and place-value reasoning.
Draw scaled picture graphs and bar graphs and solve problems using them.
Relate area of rectangles to multiplication and find area of composite figures.
Solve perimeter problems, including shapes with the same area but different perimeters.
Convert larger measurement units to smaller ones within a single system.
Solve word problems about distance, time, liquid volume, mass and money.
Find the volume of rectangular prisms by packing unit cubes and by formula.
Draw and identify points, lines, rays, angles and parallel and perpendicular lines.
Measure and sketch angles in degrees with a protractor.
Classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on their properties.
Use ordered pairs to locate points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.
Graph and interpret points in the first quadrant to solve real-world problems.
Generate two numerical patterns, compare their terms and graph the ordered pairs.
Use ratio language to describe a relationship between two quantities.
Understand unit rates and use rate language in context.
Solve ratio and rate problems with tables, double number lines, percents and unit conversions.
Recognize proportional relationships and find the constant of proportionality.
Solve multi-step ratio and percent problems such as tax, tip, discount and percent error.
Solve problems with scale drawings, computing actual lengths and areas.
Place rational numbers, including negatives, on number lines and in the coordinate plane.
Add and subtract rational numbers using number lines and additive inverses.
Multiply and divide rational numbers, explaining the sign rules with properties of operations.
Distinguish rational from irrational numbers and convert repeating decimals to fractions.
Apply the properties of integer exponents to generate equivalent expressions.
Use scientific notation to estimate and compare very large and very small quantities.
Write, read and evaluate expressions containing variables.
Apply properties of operations to produce equivalent expressions.
Solve one-step equations of the form x + p = q and px = q in real-world settings.
Add, subtract, factor and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.
Use two-step equations and inequalities to solve word problems and graph the solutions.
Solve linear equations in one variable, including those with the variable on both sides.
Graph proportional relationships and interpret unit rate as slope.
Use similar triangles to explain constant slope and derive y = mx + b.
Analyze and solve pairs of simultaneous linear equations graphically and algebraically.
Understand a function as a rule assigning exactly one output to each input.
Interpret y = mx + b as a linear function and give examples of nonlinear functions.
Construct a linear function to model a relationship and interpret its rate of change and initial value.
Find areas of triangles and special quadrilaterals by composing and decomposing shapes.
Know and use formulas for area and circumference of a circle.
Use supplementary, complementary, vertical and adjacent angles to find unknown angles.
Establish facts about angle sums, exterior angles and angles from parallel lines cut by a transversal.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find unknown side lengths in real-world and mathematical problems.
Use volume formulas for cones, cylinders and spheres to solve problems.
Summarize numerical data sets with measures of center, spread and overall shape.
Understand that random samples support valid inferences about a population.
Develop probability models and compare predicted with observed frequencies.
Find probabilities of compound events using lists, tables, tree diagrams and simulation.
Construct and interpret scatter plots, describing clustering, outliers and association.
Use the equation of a linear model to interpret slope and intercept in bivariate data.
Justify each step in solving an equation and build a viable argument for the solution.
Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, as in solving literal equations.
Use function notation, evaluate functions and interpret statements in context.
Interpret key features of graphs and tables of a function modeling a relationship.
Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately, including by elimination.
Graph solutions to linear inequalities and systems of inequalities as half-planes.
Rewrite expressions using the properties of rational exponents and radicals.
Distinguish situations modeled by linear functions from those modeled by exponential functions.
Add, subtract and multiply polynomials, understanding they form a closed system.
Use the structure of an expression to rewrite it, as in factoring a difference of squares.
Solve quadratic equations by inspection, square roots, completing the square, the formula and factoring.
Graph functions and show key features such as intercepts, maxima and minima.
Use rigid motions to decide whether two figures are congruent.
Explain how the ASA, SAS and SSS criteria follow from the definition of congruence.
Prove theorems about lines and angles, including those about parallel lines and a transversal.
Prove theorems about triangles, such as angle sum, base angles and the midsegment theorem.
Prove theorems about parallelograms and their sides, angles and diagonals.
Make formal geometric constructions with compass and straightedge or other tools.
Use similarity transformations to decide whether two figures are similar.
Use congruence and similarity criteria to solve problems and prove relationships in figures.
Use trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean theorem to solve right triangles in applied problems.
Identify and use relationships among inscribed angles, radii, chords and tangents.
Derive arc length and sector area and define the radian measure of an angle.
Use volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres to solve problems.
Represent data with dot plots, histograms and box plots.
Compare center and spread of two or more data sets using appropriate statistics.
Summarize categorical data in two-way frequency tables and interpret relative frequencies.
Fit a function to two-variable data and assess the fit by plotting residuals.
Compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit using technology.
Distinguish between correlation and causation.
Know the fundamental theorem of algebra and show it holds for quadratic polynomials.
Know and apply the remainder theorem when dividing polynomials.
Find zeros of polynomials by factoring and use them to sketch a rough graph.
Rewrite rational expressions in different forms using inspection, long division or technology.
Solve rational and radical equations and identify extraneous solutions.
Find inverse functions and write an expression for the inverse.
Express solutions to exponential equations as logarithms and evaluate them with technology.
Interpret the parameters of a linear or exponential function in context.
Understand radian measure as the arc length subtended on the unit circle.
Use the unit circle to extend trigonometric functions to all real numbers.
Model periodic phenomena with trigonometric functions using amplitude, frequency and midline.
Prove the Pythagorean identity and use it to find trigonometric values.
Recognize sequences as functions, sometimes defined recursively, on a subset of the integers.
Write arithmetic and geometric sequences recursively and explicitly and use them to model.
Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series and apply it to problems.
Build a function that models a relationship, including by combining functions.
Describe the effect of transformations such as f(x) + k and f(kx) on a graph.
Fit a function to data, use it to solve problems and assess the fit.
Use the mean and standard deviation of a normal distribution to estimate percentages.
Build two-way frequency tables and use them to decide independence and find conditional probabilities.
Understand statistics as making inferences about a population from a random sample.
Recognize the purposes of and differences among surveys, experiments and observational studies.
Use sample data to estimate a population parameter and develop a margin of error with simulation.
Evaluate reports based on data.
Use the geometric-series formula to solve problems such as computing loan payments.
Recognize when a quantity grows by a constant rate versus a constant percent, as with interest.
Interpret the parameters of a linear or exponential model in a financial context.
Use units to guide the solution of multi-step problems and to interpret graphs and data displays.
Choose a level of accuracy appropriate to the limits of measurement when reporting quantities.
Represent constraints with equations or inequalities and interpret solutions in a modeling context.
